title: Partition Key Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
Event Streaming
Kafka Partitions
Partition Key
Message Ordering
description: A p5.js simulator that routes bursts of xAPI statements into event-stream partitions by hashing a district key, a district-and-learner key or no key, so learners can compare per-partition load with the order in which the processor reads each learner's statements.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Choosing the event-stream partition key: load balance versus per-learner order
learningObjectives: The learner will compare keying by district with keying by district and learner, in terms of per-partition load and per-learner ordering.
prerequisites: The role of the event stream in the full LRS (Chapter 20)
The idea of a hash function
Why the order of evidence matters to sequential mastery updates (Chapter 18)

accessibility.notes: Radio, sliders and buttons are native controls with aria labels; the selected learner is marked by outline and sequence numbers, not color alone; overflow is shown with a +N count and a red limit tick

controls.label: Key: district only / Key: district and learner / No key (random lane)
Learner dots
controls.purpose: Select a learner to see their read order

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison of two designs on two criteria
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Switch the key, observe lane load and a learner's read order, vary parameters
keyQuestions: Which key concentrates a whole district on one partition, and why?
Does keying by district and learner give up per-learner order?
What would happen to mastery estimates if one learner's statements were read out of order?
commonMisconceptions: A coarser key gives stronger ordering guarantees
More partitions always spread a single key's traffic
assessmentOpportunities: A two-key comparison table of peak load and order

assumptions: District A holds half the learners, then 25%, 15% and 10%
Each learner sends about the same number of statements per burst
Each lane's consumer reads at a slightly different fixed pace
limitations: The limit line is a teaching threshold, not a broker setting
Broker quotas that bound each district's throughput are not modeled
Learner colors cannot all be distinct for color-blind viewers at 60 learners; selection uses outline and numbers
